items.title: Batteries the key to unlocking an energy revolution, and one state is racing ahead
items.description: Western Australia in particular is proving to the world that grid-scale batteries are no longer a complementary technology but can play a central role in power grids.

items.title: Battery boom marks a new political chapter in Australia's energy wars
items.description: Within the government, there's quiet confidence the battery boom will continue to gather pace and help shield Australia from both global shocks and domestic demand surges, driving prices even lower.

items.title: Labor's CGT challenge deepens as biotech sector raises alarm
items.description: Another sector has called for a capital gains tax change carve-out, warning the government that it will face a talent drain without it.

items.title: Israel warns all residents in southern Lebanon to leave
items.description: It is the first time Israel has made such a sweeping demand since US President Donald Trump announced in April a ceasefire had been imposed in Lebanon.

items.title: How Australia led the charge for the world to ban social media for kids
items.description: The UK could become the latest nation to implement a social media ban, after British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer vowed to introduce a "game changer" policy.

items.title: Young saviour and an answered prayer deliver Blues incredible Origin win
items.description: When the Blues needed heroes to get on top of the Maroons in State of Origin I, they turned to a debutante and the oldest player on the field.

items.title: Iran's internet is back on. But it's not what it used to be
items.description: Reports of an increase in internet traffic are filtering through, but experts say Iran has a long way to go to get back up to speed.

items.title: Trump says US 'not satisfied' with Iran peace deal proposals
items.description: It comes as the White House rejects a draft deal being reported by Iranian state TV as a "fabrication".

items.title: 'We need to talk about sex': Young people call for sex ed to grow up
items.description: A long-running survey of Australian teens has identified falling condom use and unwanted sex as major concerns for young people starting relationships.

items.title: UK spy chief says 500,000 Russians killed in Ukraine war so far
items.description: The head of a major UK intelligence agency is warning that Moscow and other adversaries could use artificial intelligence and other emerging technology to conduct "hybrid warfare" against western allies.

items.title: Matthew Perry's assistant jailed for role in Friends actor's death
items.description: Matthew Perry's live-in personal assistant, who had a central role in the Friends star's descent into ketamine addiction and injected him with the fatal dose of the drug, has been sentenced to three years and five months in prison.

items.title: Video shows divers finding five Laos cavers alive, two remain missing
items.description: A rescue mission has been underway for more than a week to find seven people who entered a cave in central Laos before becoming trapped in a landslide triggered by heavy rain.

items.title: Fears Melbourne man met with foul play on trip to India
items.description: The family of maths teacher Sunil Sharma say the 66-year-old disappeared nearly a week ago, while trying to sell a property in the Punjabi city of Amritsar.

items.title: 'To embarrass me?': Apology demanded over leak to media of personal information
items.description: A Tasmanian independent politician is calling for an apology after her personal health-related request via email to the government was leaked to a media outlet.

items.title: Why this photo has been terrifying the internet for years
items.description: Forget about slashers and body horror — the next evolution of fright stems from an fluorescent-lit room.

items.title: Pop art-inspired willy wagtails taking flight beyond Surf Coast
items.description: A Victorian artist paints hundreds of willie wagtails a week to give away locally and now they're popping up all over the world.

items.title: Quiz: Can you identify Aussie TV shows from a single frame?
items.description: How well do you know your Neighbours from your Deadloch? Take our single-frame Australian TV quiz to find out.

items.title: Can farmers become less reliant on synthetic fertiliser? Some are trying
items.description: A war thousands of kilometres away from Australia's farms is quietly reshaping what crops are planted and what will be available at supermarkets in the future.

items.title: As the debate heats up, migrants are quietly keeping the bush running
items.description: Amid ongoing discussion about Australia's immigration intake and migration policies, regional residents say many industries in the bush cannot survive without overseas workers.

items.title: What we know, and what we don't, about new changes to Centrelink system
items.description: The federal government has proposed changes to Australia's $2 billion employment services system to make them “more responsive, effective and dignified”.

items.title: Chalmers flags 'legitimate' small business CGT debate
items.description: The government is treading carefully on carve-outs to its capital gains tax legislation amid backlash to its plan.

items.title: Bondi shooting victim labelled 'subhuman' in online abuse of inquiry witnesses
items.description: Victims of antisemitism have been targeted with death threats and depicted as animals in AI-generated images after giving evidence to the royal commission examining the Bondi terror attack.

items.title: PM response to truth-telling process 'hugely significant'
items.description: The Walk for Truth ended at Parliament House today and while there was not a firm commitment from the PM, many felt the response was a 'positive move'.

items.title: FIFA faces investigation over 'impossibly high' World Cup ticket prices
items.description: In a joint statement, New Jersey's attorney-general accused the football governing body of having turned "buying a ticket to the World Cup into a gauntlet of confusion, fake scarcity, and impossibly high prices".

items.title: ISIS-linked woman barred from Australia tried to board flight
items.description: An Australian woman with links to ISIS, who is barred from Australia on a temporary exclusion order, tried to board a flight home with the other members of Tuesday's returning cohort, a Senate estimates hearing has been told.
